title: DragTraffic: Interactive and Controllable Traffic Scene Generation for Autonomous Driving

control_signal.value: User-specified context per agent: vehicle type, length and width, start position/speed/orientation, target position/speed/orientation, set by dragging or typing; can be taken from the dataset instead.

control_mechanism.value: Context is fed into the diffusion denoiser via cross-attention; an MLP encodes the 8-dim condition and concatenates it with state and lane encoders in the initializer regression model. No guidance loss.

base_model.value: MultiPath++ regression model gives initial trajectory; conditional U-Net diffusion refines it (5 denoising steps); mixture-of-experts gate selects a model per agent type.

datasets.value: Waymo Open Dataset (about 70,000 scenarios) cut into 6-second clips; ego-, cyclist-, pedestrian-centered subsets of 49,884, 29,046 and 9,344 cases; 80/10/10 split.

metrics.value: Scenario collision rate (SCR); open-loop MinADE6, MinFDE6, heading error, speed error.

controllability_evidence.value: Interaction reasoning: SCR at 9s rollout is 3.33% for DragTraffic with condition vs 13.59% for TrafficGen mixture training. Qualitative scene editing: setting agent 1's target condition removes its freezing.

stated_limitations.value: Future work: post-processing or sampling so actions obey dynamic constraints; multi-round generation with human feedback. Weak on the cyclist subset, possibly due to few cyclists.

notes: Controllability evidence is mostly qualitative figures; no quantitative condition-adherence metric in the packet.
